takeaways: The AI sector faces a systemic correction as Nvidia’s leadership transition and SEC probe trigger a broader sell-off, erasing year-to-date gains for the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

Regulatory and geopolitical headwinds are intensifying, with proposed domestic-only data center mandates and stricter export controls creating significant operational friction for global tech infrastructure expansion.
Market sentiment has shifted toward defensive positioning, evidenced by a flight to Treasury bonds as investors question the sustainability of massive AI capital expenditures amid cooling growth.
day_verdict: Today is a read-carefully day as a massive market sell-off, triggered by the shock resignation of Nvidia's CEO and a new SEC accounting probe, has sent major indices and tech stocks into a sharp correction.

items.title: 6 reasons stocks are falling, and what you should do about it
bullets: The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index plummeted 5.3% in a single session, marking its second-worst performance of 2026 and effectively erasing all year-to-date gains for the index.

Investors are increasingly skeptical of the massive capital expenditure on AI infrastructure, as evidenced by Anthropic's reported $104 billion loss in the first nine months of 2026 despite rapid revenue growth.
items.reason: Market-wide correction driven by fundamental concerns over AI profitability.

items.title: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on tech companies building data centers outside the US
bullets: President-elect Trump has signaled intent to impose significant tax penalties on U.S. technology firms that construct AI data centers in foreign jurisdictions, citing domestic community opposition and national interests.

This policy shift creates material regulatory risk for Big Tech, as companies rely on global infrastructure expansion to meet the massive power and compute demands required for large-scale AI development.
items.reason: Significant regulatory risk impacting the capital expenditure strategy of major tech firms.

items.title: Cognition in talks for new funding at $75 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reports
bullets: The AI startup Cognition is reportedly in discussions for a new funding round that would value the company at $75 billion, signaling continued aggressive capital allocation toward foundational AI models.
This valuation reflects the intense investor appetite for high-growth AI infrastructure and development firms, potentially setting a new benchmark for private market valuations in the sector.
items.reason: Significant valuation milestone for a major AI player.

items.title: Senator proposes select committee on AI as Democrats hope to move quickly to regulate it
bullets: A proposal to establish a select committee on AI indicates that legislative efforts to regulate the industry are gaining momentum, which could introduce new compliance costs and operational constraints for tech firms.
Investors should monitor this development as a potential precursor to formal federal oversight, which may impact the deployment strategies and long-term profitability of AI-focused enterprises.
items.reason: Regulatory shifts create material risks for AI investments.

items.title: U.S. Cleared Nearly 880,000 AI Chips for Chinese Buyers
bullets: The U.S. government has approved the export of nearly 880,000 AI-capable chips to Chinese entities, highlighting a significant volume of high-end hardware still reaching the Chinese market despite tightening restrictions.

This data suggests that while export controls are in place, the scale of approved shipments remains substantial, potentially impacting the competitive landscape for AI development and the efficacy of current U.S. containment strategies.
items.reason: Quantifies the scale of chip exports to China, directly impacting semiconductor supply chain and AI policy analysis.

items.title: Nvidia faces further blow after shock US export permit data release: analysts
bullets: Analysts indicate that the recent disclosure of export permit data creates additional regulatory and reputational pressure for Nvidia, as scrutiny intensifies regarding the flow of its technology to Chinese markets.

The combination of export permit transparency and ongoing geopolitical tensions creates a volatile environment for Nvidia's revenue projections, as investors weigh the risk of further tightening of U.S. trade policies.
items.reason: Directly impacts the market valuation and regulatory outlook for the most critical company in the AI hardware sector.

items.title: BMO demonstrates quantum computing milestone for AI and machine learning
bullets: BMO achieved a 'quantum utility' milestone by using quantum processors to perform feature selection in machine learning, demonstrating that quantum systems can identify relevant variables in complex datasets more efficiently than classical methods.

The application required one to two orders of magnitude fewer data samples than traditional techniques, signaling a potential path for financial institutions to optimize AI models for fraud detection and risk management with significantly reduced data overhead.
items.reason: Demonstrates practical, scalable quantum-AI integration in finance.

items.title: New approach enables physically consistent AI models of chaotic systems
bullets: MIT researchers developed a method to enforce physics-based constraints on machine learning models, preventing them from drifting into physically impossible predictions when modeling chaotic systems like weather, ocean currents, or turbulent flows.

By ensuring models remain bounded by real-world physical laws, this innovation enhances the reliability of AI for industrial, aeronautical, and climate-related forecasting, reducing the risk of catastrophic errors in data-driven decision-making systems.
items.reason: Addresses a critical reliability gap in AI modeling for industrial and environmental applications.

items.title: Nvidia Said to Face S.E.C. Probe Into Its Accounting Practices
bullets: The SEC has initiated an investigation into Nvidia's accounting practices, a development that has significantly contributed to the company's recent market valuation decline.
This regulatory scrutiny adds a layer of legal and financial uncertainty for investors, potentially impacting the company's future reporting transparency and long-term stock stability.
items.reason: Regulatory investigations into accounting practices represent a high-impact risk for shareholders.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. What happens next?
bullets: The resignation of Jensen Huang marks a pivotal leadership transition for Nvidia, raising questions about the company's strategic direction and its ability to maintain its dominant position in the AI hardware market.

The departure has triggered significant market volatility, with the stock experiencing massive sell-offs as investors reassess the company's valuation in the absence of its long-time visionary leader.
items.reason: The sudden departure of a founder-CEO is a fundamental shift in corporate governance and strategy.

items.title: Tesla’s U.S. Sales Tanked In Q1. It Still Gained Market Share
bullets: Tesla's U.S. sales declined 8.4% year-over-year to 117,300 units in Q1 2026, marking the company's lowest quarterly performance since late 2021.
Despite the volume drop, Tesla's market share expanded from 43.2% to 54.2% as the broader U.S. EV market contracted by 27%, with non-Tesla sales falling 41%.
items.reason: Significant market share shift despite industry-wide contraction

items.title: Japan's METI Closes EV Subsidy Applications Early as Budget Balance Dwindles to ¥930 Million
bullets: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry abruptly halted EV subsidy applications on November 20 after the ¥110 billion budget was nearly exhausted by higher-than-expected demand.

The program, which offered up to ¥1.3 million per vehicle, was a key driver for EV adoption; its early closure creates immediate uncertainty for manufacturers relying on these incentives to maintain sales momentum.
items.reason: Sudden policy shift impacting EV demand in a major market

items.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
bullets: President Trump has threatened to impose a 'tremendous tax' on US companies that construct AI data centers outside of the country, citing national security concerns regarding China's access to computing power.

The proposed policy aims to force domestic infrastructure development, potentially disrupting the global expansion strategies of major tech firms like Meta and Google that have already secured international data center agreements.
items.reason: Significant regulatory risk to hyperscalers and global AI infrastructure strategy.

items.title: Bloom Energy (BE) Says Its Fuel Cells Can Power AI Data Centers Within Months
bullets: Bloom Energy is positioning its modular solid oxide fuel cell systems as a critical solution for AI data centers to bypass multi-year utility grid interconnection queues and begin operations within months.

Investors should monitor the company's ability to convert this immediate power pitch into a measurable backlog, as future revenue growth depends on securing firm multi-year service contracts with hyperscalers.
items.reason: Direct solution to the primary bottleneck (power) facing the AI data center industry.

items.title: Project Saturn: 5 Lenders Seek SpaceX Chip Launch Ban
bullets: Lenders involved in a $43 billion debt package for SpaceX have reportedly sought contractual safeguards to prevent AI chips pledged as collateral from being deployed into orbital facilities. This unusual request highlights lender anxiety regarding the recoverability of high-value hardware assets that are physically inaccessible once launched into space.

While SpaceX maintains that the financed hardware is intended for terrestrial data centers, the negotiation underscores the complex intersection of AI infrastructure financing and space-based compute ambitions. The potential for such restrictive covenants could impact future capital-raising flexibility for companies attempting to bridge the gap between terrestrial AI training and orbital operations.
items.reason: Significant financial implications for a major private space entity's debt structure.

items.title: Japan to transfer H3 rocket launch operations to Mitsubishi Heavy
bullets: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) is transitioning H3 rocket launch operations to Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, a strategic move designed to commercialize the platform and improve operational efficiency. This shift allows the national agency to pivot its resources toward advanced rocket development and next-generation space exploration technologies.

For investors, this privatization of launch services signals a maturation of Japan's domestic space industry, potentially lowering costs and increasing launch cadence for commercial satellite operators. The move aligns with global trends of outsourcing routine space logistics to private contractors to foster a more competitive and sustainable aerospace ecosystem.
items.reason: Major structural shift in national space policy with long-term commercial impact.

items.title: Shopping, chips and central banks
bullets: The National Retail Federation forecasts a 4.2% increase in US holiday spending for November and December, reaching a total of $1.013 trillion despite concerns over high borrowing costs.
Investors are closely monitoring upcoming US GDP data and inflation reports alongside central bank interest rate decisions in South Korea, Australia, and Japan to gauge global economic health.
items.reason: Covers critical US consumer spending data and global central bank policy shifts.

items.title: ECB to make euro swaps more accessible in global push, Lagarde says
bullets: ECB President Christine Lagarde announced plans to expand currency swap lines to enhance the euro's global role and protect the euro area from external financial shocks.

The initiative aims to reduce reliance on the US dollar for trade and investment, while providing reserve managers with greater liquidity assurance to support the holding of euro-denominated securities.
items.reason: Significant strategic shift in ECB policy regarding global currency dominance.

items.title: Central Bank hikes policy rate to 9% as inflation surges
bullets: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has raised its key policy rate to 9% in response to surging inflation and rapid credit growth within the domestic economy.
This aggressive monetary tightening reflects the ongoing struggle of emerging markets to balance economic stability against the pressures of rising global price levels.
items.reason: Important indicator of monetary policy tightening in emerging market economies.

items.title: S&P 500 correction: Five forces behind the market sell-off
bullets: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average have officially entered correction territory, defined as a decline of more than 10% from recent record highs, while the Nasdaq Composite has erased all gains for the year.

Market sentiment has soured due to a perceived 'sell the news' event surrounding the Anthropic IPO and a significant 14% single-day drop in Nvidia shares, which were further pressured by reports of an SEC accounting probe.
items.reason: Market-wide correction and major tech sector volatility

items.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 20: Nvidia's $2.5 Trillion Rout Deepens as SEC Accounting Probe Adds to Wall Street's AI Sell-Off
bullets: Nvidia has experienced a massive $2.5 trillion valuation decline, with shares dropping nearly 40% in November alone amid mounting regulatory and leadership crises.
The company is facing intense scrutiny following reports of an SEC probe into its accounting practices, compounding investor fears regarding the sustainability of the broader AI-driven bull market.
items.reason: Specific catalyst for the broader tech sector sell-off

items.title: Treasury yields move sharply lower as investors flee to safe havens
bullets: The 10-year Treasury yield dropped 12 basis points to 4.932%, while the 2-year note yield fell over 14 basis points to 4.634% as market volatility triggered a flight to safety.
Despite the rally in bond prices, traders continue to price in a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, reflecting persistent concerns over inflation and hawkish Fed rhetoric.
items.reason: Significant market-wide repricing of risk and interest rate expectations.

items.title: The Weekly Spread: What Shaped US Treasury Yields And The Dollar This Week
bullets: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield declined 20 basis points over the week to 4.95%, as investors questioned the sustainability of AI-driven capital expenditure and rotated into government debt.

Market sentiment shifted toward defensive positioning, evidenced by the iShares 1-3 year ETF (SHY) recording its best weekly performance since August 2024, signaling strong demand for short-duration safe-haven assets.
items.reason: Comprehensive summary of weekly fixed income trends and investor sentiment shifts.

items.title: Officials approved the sale of 580,000 Nvidia chips to Chinese companies
bullets: The approval of 580,000 Nvidia chips for export to China represents a significant volume of high-performance hardware, potentially impacting the competitive landscape for AI development in the region.
This massive authorization highlights a complex regulatory environment where U.S. officials are balancing national security concerns against the commercial interests of domestic semiconductor giants.
items.reason: Direct impact on major tech stock supply chains and geopolitical trade policy.

items.title: U.S. Government Establishes Export Controls to Address China AI “Remote Access” Concerns
bullets: New export controls targeting 'remote access' to AI capabilities suggest a shift in U.S. strategy to prevent Chinese entities from bypassing hardware restrictions via cloud-based infrastructure.
Investors should anticipate increased compliance costs and operational friction for cloud service providers and AI firms that maintain cross-border data and computing service agreements.
items.reason: Signals a tightening of regulatory loopholes that could affect global cloud and AI business models.

items.title: Hongkong Land raises full-year earnings guidance as Q3 underlying profit rises 38%
bullets: The developer upgraded its FY2026 underlying profit outlook to a 'mid-teens' percentage increase, driven by strong performance in its Hong Kong Central portfolio and mainland China assets.

Operational efficiency is improving, with office vacancy rates in the Central portfolio falling below 5% for the first time since 2022, signaling a recovery in leasing momentum and positive rental reversions.
items.reason: Significant earnings guidance upgrade for a major blue-chip property developer.

items.title: Hong Kong secondary home price index falls for sixth straight week to six-month low
bullets: The secondary residential market continues to face downward pressure, with the price index hitting a six-month low following six consecutive weeks of decline.
This persistent trend suggests ongoing weakness in the property sector, reflecting broader investor caution and potential challenges for household wealth and mortgage-related financial stability.
items.reason: Key indicator of ongoing weakness in the crucial Hong Kong residential property market.
